objective: TIME-POLISH PPO on Jungle2: start from the bc49 panorama BC student and optimize EXPECTED COMPLETION TIME with the recipe that achieved tier_1 on Jungle1 (lineage.recipe_validation: student median 3058 beat teacher 3134 at 16/16, concluded by the preregistered stagnation clause). HONEST EVIDENCE DELTA versus both prior premises: the Jungle1 init carried a 10,000-seed tail receipt (98.56% win rate) and the Jungle4 init carried 8/8 panorama wins; THIS init won 4/8 on the panorama gate (hold 8, max_ticks 30000) and 8/16 = 0.5000 on the exact 16-seed checkpoint panel measured at hold 4 BEFORE this freeze (median winning ticks 10920.0; lineage.init_baseline_panel16). Half the panel is unwon at init, so this run is asked to do real work on BOTH axes - keep (or grow) the win rate while pulling the winning-tick median down - and the relative floor of clause (a) (max(0.50, 0.5000 - 0.05) = 0.50) is calibrated so that the run is stopped only for degrading BELOW its own receipted starting point, not for failing to meet a bar the init never held (the exact failure mode of the jungle8 stop, lineage.floor_lesson). The premise stands on the validated Jungle1 mechanism: when the +10 win bonus appears in most episodes, the return's residual variance is dominated by the 5x time term (-0.0005/native tick) and PPO polishes speed instead of searching for wins; with wins at only 0.50 the win-search gradient is live too, and the truncation-neutral wrapper plus the win-dominance ordering (worst win +4.0 > best failure -9.0) point it the right way. Success is measured in median winning ticks at a win-rate floor; SCORE IS NOT A SUCCESS METRIC.

reward_resolution.how_the_validator_resolves_it: carried verbatim from the pattern document (the resolution path is unchanged): v2._configs_v2 hands environment.reward_profile to v2._reward_config_v2; each of profile_id, win_reward, failure_reward, time_penalty_per_native_tick present in the mapping OVERRIDES the v2 defaults; score_progress_reward_cap is owned by TrainerV2Config (trainer_v2.score_progress_reward_cap, here 1.0). profile_id is a label checked only for non-emptiness; the id win-time5x-score-truncation-neutral-v3 is REUSED because the profile it names is bitwise the same profile.
reward_resolution.ordering_guarantees: the composed training wrapper is DenseShapingObservableHumanSpeedrunWrapper; its _validate_reward_ordering enforces minimum win return > maximum terminated-failure return: (10 + (-0.0005 x 12000)) = +4.0 > (-10 + 1.0) = -9.0, satisfied with margin 13.0 at Jungle2's max_ticks 12000 (identical arithmetic to the pattern: jungle levels are not in the long-horizon prefix list). The base-wrapper one-second dominance rule is deliberately dropped by the v2 dense-shaping mixin, exactly as documented in the pattern.
reward_resolution.magnitude_rationale: 5x clock signal, unchanged from the validated recipe. At the measured panel median (10920 ticks, hold 4, max_ticks 30000) the time term costs ~-5.5 against +10; at the training horizon the worst POSSIBLE win costs -6.0, still netting +4.0, so winning strictly dominates everything and the residual gradient on winning episodes is the clock. A 500-tick speedup is worth +0.25 per episode, the same well-posed polish signal that took Jungle1 from median 3833 to 3058.

early_stop_rules.checkpoint_grid_note: checkpoint_every 262144 with 40 envs -> SB3 CheckpointCallback save_freq = 262144 // 40 = 6553 vec-steps, i.e. checkpoints on a 262,120-macro-step grid: 7 checkpoints inside the 2M budget (262120, 524240, 786360, 1048480, 1310600, 1572720, 1834840); each checkpoint gets the 16-seed eval below before the next checkpoint lands. The Jungle1 champion emerged at checkpoint 1572720, inside this grid.
early_stop_rules.checkpoint_eval_protocol: 16-seed held-out panel, seeds 1494001000..1494001015, level Jungle2, hold_ticks 4, stack lags 0,4,8, deterministic masked predict, via tools/probe_alphazuma_55_macro_native_eval_v1.py (sha256:f36c6af8ebb481f21736f9a4fb79538463a27b69edb450b51d428193a290c23d) run ONE SEED PER INVOCATION at the probe's default max_ticks 30000 into eval16-ckpt<N>/seed-<seed> run dirs - the protocol is bit-for-bit the init-baseline protocol (lineage.init_baseline_panel16) and matches every eval16-* receipt already in this campaign; eval device chosen at eval time so as not to preempt training (this run holds cuda:1); metrics recorded: wins/16, median winning ticks over the wins, shots_on_target_rate

clause_a_win_rate_floor.clause: if the 16-seed eval win rate is below 0.50 (i.e. 7/16 or fewer wins) at TWO CONSECUTIVE checkpoints, STOP the run and keep the best earlier checkpoint. The floor is max(0.50, 0.5000 - 0.05) = 0.50: RELATIVE to the measured init baseline of 8/16 = 0.5000 (lineage.init_baseline_panel16), with the 0.50 hard floor binding because the measured rate sits exactly at it.
clause_a_win_rate_floor.best_checkpoint_rule: best = highest 16-seed win rate; ties broken by lower median winning ticks; the BC init itself is the fallback if no checkpoint qualifies - and unlike the pattern document's fallback, this init HAS a receipt on this exact panel (8/16, median 10920.0), so the fallback comparison is like-for-like by construction
clause_a_win_rate_floor.rationale: the jungle8 stop (lineage.floor_lesson) showed a fixed floor punishes the run for the init's own miss rate; this floor stops the run only for falling BELOW its receipted starting point (minus the 5pp allowance, clamped at the 0.50 hard floor). With init win evidence at exactly 0.50, the hard floor also enforces the reward-design premise that wins appear in at least half the episodes.

clause_b_stagnation_success.clause: if the median winning ticks of the 16-seed eval fails to improve on the best median observed so far at THREE CONSECUTIVE checkpoint evals, CONCLUDE THE RUN SUCCESSFULLY with the best checkpoint
clause_b_stagnation_success.best_checkpoint_rule: best = lowest median winning ticks among checkpoints whose 16-seed win rate is >= the clause (a) floor (0.50)
clause_b_stagnation_success.rationale: time-polish saturates; three flat checkpoints (~786k steps) is the preregistered definition of converged. This clause is not a hypothesis: it fired on Jungle1 exactly as designed and banked the champion. UNCHANGED from the pattern document except that its best rule references the relative floor.

trainer_v2.reward_alignment: cap 1.0 and the 5x time term carried unchanged from the validated recipe. Arithmetic at Jungle2's max_ticks 12000: worst win = 10 - 6.0 = +4.0; best truncation (truncation-neutral) = about -6.0 + 1.0 = -5.0; best terminated failure = -10 + 1.0 - time < -9.0. Ordering: every win > every truncation > every terminated failure; on winning episodes the clock is the dominant residual signal, which is the entire point of this run.
trainer_v2.discounting_note: gamma applies PER MACRO STEP; the macro reward is the undiscounted per-tick sum over the ticks the macro consumed, so 0.999 per macro is roughly 0.999^(1/40) per native tick; truncation is reward-neutral (v2 wrapper), so a timed-out episode bootstraps instead of paying -10

runs.checkpoint_note: one macro step is one policy timestep (~20-70 native ticks); with 40 envs the callback grid floors to 262,120 steps (7 checkpoints in the 2M budget). At the observed timepolish throughput the 2M budget fits well inside the 4.5-h window; the v2 callback stops at schedule.training_stop_utc regardless.

If the median is still improving at checkpoint 1834840 the run ends at the budget with the best checkpoint per clause (b)'s best rule - that outcome is reported as budget-capped, not stagnation-concluded.

Win-rate qualifiers are RELATIVE to the measured init baseline (8/16 = 0.5000), consistent with the clause (a) improvement; the pattern's fixed 0.90 qualifier is not carried.
success_criteria_tiers.tier_0_sanity: wrapper fidelity holds under the trained policy: shots_on_target_rate >= 0.95 on every checkpoint eval, and the 16-seed win rate never drops below the clause (a) floor (0.50) at the adjudicated best checkpoint
success_criteria_tiers.tier_1_beat_teacher_time: median winning ticks < 2300 (the teacher-through-macro Jungle2 time, lineage.teacher_reference, seed 1400920001) at a 16-seed win rate >= the measured init rate 0.5000 (8/16) on the best checkpoint's panel; for reference the init's own panel median is 10920.0, so tier_1 demands roughly a 4.7x median speedup without giving back any of the init's win rate
success_criteria_tiers.tier_2_any_win_under_1p5x_teacher: ANY documented eval or search win by the trained policy under 3450 ticks (1.5 x the 2300-tick teacher time); the init's fastest receipted win is 2079 ticks (panorama seed 1495002001), which already meets this bar - tier_2 for THIS run means the TRAINED policy reproduces a sub-3450 win under this document's own receipts, establishing the polish did not destroy the fast tail
